title: Weekly rollup fact tables for per-route usage, cohorts, and cost attribution
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Design and implement a set of weekly-curated fact and dimension tables that drive Console dashboards and cost reports. These tables will provide pre-aggregated, join-ready views for: 1) per-API-route usage (requests, tokens, latency P50/P95), 2) weekly user cohorts (by org, plan, and onboarding channel), and 3) cost attribution estimates per route and per-tenant using GPU-second and token consumption heuristics. We want these tables to be compact, partitioned for efficient access, and friendly to BI tooling (materialized views / read-optimized schemas). This ticket covers canonical schema, ETL transforms (dbt), SCD handling for dimensions, partitioning strategy, rollup cadence, and a minimal backfill plan for the last 90 days of data. Intended consumers: Console dashboards, billing QA, Growth analytics, and on-call SRE for anomaly detection.
acceptance_criteria: Schema with fact and dimension definitions reviewed and approved by Analytics PM and Console Backend lead
Weekly fact tables produced and accessible in analytics schema (analytics.weekly_route_facts, analytics.weekly_cohort_facts, analytics.weekly_cost_facts)
All tables partitioned by week_start_date and clustered on org_id and route_id where supported
ETL implemented in dbt with idempotent incremental runs and documented materialization configurations
Backfill for last 90 days completed without exceeding cluster resource quotas; backfill runbook committed
Validation queries comparing curried weekly aggregates to raw event aggregates pass with <0.1% variance (tolerance defined)
Owners and SLAs documented: data freshness = 24 hours, failure alerting to #analytics-pipeline channel
implementation_notes: Proposed approach: 1) Create dimension tables: dim_org (SCD2 - capture tier changes), dim_route (immutable route metadata + latest config), dim_model_variant (SCD2 to track quantization/variant). 2) Build staging tables from console_event_stream that normalize events into canonical columns (org_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, timestamp). 3) Weekly fact aggregates derived via dbt incremental models that aggregate by week_start_date and group keys (org, route, model_variant). 4) Cost attribution: apply per-token and inferred GPU-second multipliers based on model_variant profiles; capture both estimated_cost and cost_breakdown_tags. 5) Materialize light denormalized versions for BI (prefixed analytics_mv_*) to speed dashboard queries. Keep model_variant as separate SCD2 join key to enable historical queries.
data_model_changes: Add analytics.dim_model_variant (SCD2) with columns: model_id, quantization_profile, cpu_gpu_flag, effective_from, effective_to, surrogate_key
Add analytics.weekly_route_facts with measures: requests_count, tokens_in_sum, tokens_out_sum, latency_p50, latency_p95, estimated_cost_sum
Add analytics.weekly_cohort_facts aggregated by onboarding_source and subscription_tier
Introduce analytics_mv_route_costs (materialized view) denormalized for BI joins
backfill_plan: Backfill strategy: run incremental dbt seeds + models for the 90-day window in 7-day windows to control resource pressure. Steps: 1) run staging loads for raw events for window, 2) run dim model_variant and dim_org full refresh, 3) run weekly_fact models with full-refresh for target window, 4) run validation queries and spot-check samples, 5) promote to analytics schema and update ACLs. Expected cluster impact: moderate; schedule during low-usage windows with throttling and job concurrency limits. Rollback: if validation fails, restore pre-backfill table snapshots from last backup and escalate to infra.
validation_queries: Compare sum(tokens_in/out) between analytics.weekly_route_facts and raw events grouped by week_start_date, route_id: expect variance <0.1%
Compare request counts and latency percentiles computed from raw event histograms vs aggregated fields for a random sample of 50 routes
Cross-check estimated_cost_sum against billing export for top 10 orgs by spend (sanity tolerance 2%)
